elements.text: Both pilots' failure to see and avoid the other helicopter
Pilots' responsibility to perform reporting and visual tracking duties for ENG operations
Lack of formal procedures for Phoenix-area ENG pilots regarding these operations
Pilots' reporting and visual tracking duties precluded them from recognizing helicopter proximity
One or both pilots lost awareness of the other helicopter's position
Pilots were properly certificated and qualified
Helicopters were properly certified, equipped, and maintained
No evidence of preimpact structural, engine, or system failures
Sun glare did not interfere with detection
Color vision deficiency was not a factor
Lack of information precluded precise determination of events
Limitations of see-and-avoid concept in high-density traffic with nonflying duties
High-visibility paint or lights could have facilitated detection
Traffic advisory system would enhance detection capability
Annual meetings with local ENG and FAA personnel would improve safety
Best practice guidelines would provide practical knowledge
Recorder systems would have aided investigators
